name: Cabo Verde
summary: Atlantic islands off West Africa, uninhabited until the Portuguese arrived in 1456; a hub of the Atlantic slave trade, independent in 1975, and now one of Africa’s most stable democracies.

knownFor.label: Morna
knownFor.note: Sad songs made famous by Cesária Évora.

knownFor.label: Cidade Velha
knownFor.note: First European colonial town in the tropics.

location.value: Atlantic Ocean, about 570 km off West Africa; area 4,033 km².

terrain.value: Ten volcanic islands; Sal, Boa Vista and Maio are flat, sandy and dry, and less than 2% of land is arable.

climate.value: Semi-arid, with irregular rain that falls mainly from August to October.

resources.value: Fish and tourism; the islands have few natural resources and little rainfall.

disasters.value: Famines during the droughts of the 1940s killed tens of thousands.

urbanisation.value: Praia, on Santiago island, is the largest city, with about 138,000 people (2021).

disease.value: Six hospitals and 28 health centres; life expectancy 76.2 (2017).

migration.value: Nearly one million live abroad, mostly in the United States (about 500,000) and Portugal (about 150,000).

economicBase.value: Services (commerce, transport, public services) make up over 70% of GDP; remittances are about 20% of GDP; tourism is growing; fishing is small.

tradeRoutes.value: Shipping and flights link the islands to Portugal, Europe and the Americas.

wealth.value: A middle-income country: the UN has classed it as middle income since 2008.

moneyAndTax.value: The Cape Verdean escudo, pegged to the euro.

inequality.value: Medium inequality: Gini index 42.4 (2015). The source does not describe the gap between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A semi-presidential republic, with a National Assembly elected for five-year terms.

keyRulers.value: Aristides Pereira. Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Elections have led to peaceful changes of government since 1991.

institutions.value: A National Assembly, a president and independent courts.

stability.value: A stable representative democracy since the early 1990s.

eliteConflict.value: Two main parties: PAICV and MpD.

armyAndTech.value: A National Guard and a Coast Guard.

majorWars.value: No wars since independence; the armed forces' only battles were in the independence war (1974–75).

alliancesRivals.value: Close cooperation with Portugal, including a currency once linked to the Portuguese escudo.

inventions.value: No major inventions are recorded; Cabo Verde is better known for morna music.

openness.value: Open to trade and travel, with a large diaspora abroad.

communicationTransport.value: Ferries and flights link the ten islands.

religion.value: Mostly Christian (81.7%, 2021), with 72.5% Catholic (2021); Islam is the largest minority.

languageWriting.value: Portuguese is official; Cape Verdean Creole is the national language and mother tongue of virtually all Cape Verdeans.

artsArchitecture.value: Morna and funaná music, and the colonial towns of Cidade Velha, a World Heritage Site.

socialStructure.value: Descended from Africans and from Europeans of various origins.

sharedIdentity.value: A shared island identity and Creole language, with a large diaspora in the United States and Portugal.

dailyLife.value: Cachupa, a slow-cooked stew of corn, beans and fish or meat.

neighbours.value: No land borders; the islands lie near Senegal, The Gambia and Mauritania.

colonisation.value: Portuguese settlement at Ribeira Grande from 1462; independence granted 1975.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Cabo Verde continues as an independent republic.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
